title: Effect of Sintering Temperature on the Microstructure and Integrated Properties of MgAlTiVFeCo Lightweight High-Entropy Alloy

recollection.starting_material: Guess: Near-equiatomic elemental powders of Mg, Al, Ti, V, Fe, and Co (often blended under Ar with a slight Mg excess to compensate for volatilization), used as the feedstock for powder metallurgy.
recollection.intervention: Guess: High-energy mechanical alloying of the elemental powders followed by spark plasma sintering under vacuum/inert gas at different sintering temperatures (roughly 600–950 °C), with a uniaxial pressure ~40–50 MPa and short holds (5–10 min) to study temperature effects; some studies also vary dwell to balance densification and Mg loss.
recollection.structure: Guess: A temperature-dependent evolution from a partially transformed mixture at low T to a dense dual-phase BCC-based microstructure at intermediate T, specifically disordered BCC (A2) plus ordered B2, with nano- to submicron Laves-type intermetallics ((Ti,V)-(Fe,Co)2) decorating grain boundaries; at the highest T, grain coarsening, increased B2 ordering and coarsened Laves precipitates appear, along with localized porosity from Mg evaporation.
recollection.mechanism: Guess: Competition between high-entropy stabilization of a disordered BCC solid solution and enthalpy-driven ordering/IMC formation. Increasing T accelerates diffusion, completing solid-solution formation and densification first; further T promotes B2 ordering and Laves precipitation. Mg’s low boiling/melting points cause volatilization at high T, shifting composition and introducing pores, which degrades properties beyond an optimal sintering window.
recollection.results: Guess: Relative density rises from ~92–95% at ~600–650 °C (incomplete necking, residual porosity) to ~98–99% at ~800–850 °C, then slightly drops (~96–97%) at ≥900 °C due to Mg loss. Grain size grows from a few micrometers at low T to ~10–20 µm at high T. Vickers hardness increases with densification and B2/Laves precipitation, peaking around 550–600 HV at ~800–850 °C (from ~380–450 HV at low T), then softens modestly with coarsening (≈500 HV at ~950 °C). Room-temperature uniaxial compression shows highest strength/ductility near the optimal T: compressive yield ~1.3–1.5 GPa and ultimate ~1.8–2.0 GPa with plastic strain ~10–15%; at low T, strength is lower (~0.9–1.2 GPa) and ductility limited (~4–6%) from porosity; at the highest T, strength drops slightly (~1.5–1.7 GPa) and ductility ~8–10% due to coarsening and Mg-related porosity. Fracture surfaces transition from brittle cleavage-dominated at low T to mixed cleavage/microvoid coalescence at optimal T, reverting toward more brittle features at the highest T. The best integrated properties are achieved at an intermediate sintering temperature window (≈800–850 °C).

score.note: The recollection correctly identifies SPS and gives a high-temperature density estimate close to the actual 96.7%, but it incorrectly places the optimum at 800–850 °C rather than 1000 °C. Its proposed BCC/B2/Laves microstructure conflicts with the reported dense oxide-barrier-phase microstructure. It also misses the passive-film/Cl− blocking corrosion mechanism and parabolic diffusion-controlled oxidation. Hardness is substantially underestimated, and the actual oxidation and corrosion values are absent.
